A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Collab-Overcooked research and contain 30 readable pages, including Appendices A–C. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 11 LLMs, experiments with 10 human participants, attention interventions, and collaboration failure analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs and retains the human experiments, attention interventions, and supplementary failure analyses.

M1.justification: The resource-isolated, asymmetric-knowledge environment and the agent architecture remain unchanged. Sections 4.2 and A.3 retain the same planning, communication, memory, reflection, and error-handling components; expanded explanations do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 30 cooking tasks across six complexity levels and retain the same human, attention, and sequential collaboration scenarios. Table 5's task coverage is unchanged; adding evaluated LLMs does not add tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Claude Sonnet 4 and o4-mini, expanding the evaluated model set from 11 to 13. Figure 3 also adds these models but omits DeepSeek-R1 from that comparison, although it remains in Table 2 and Figure 4. Other model-name changes are cosmetic.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4.3's Listing 6 changes the reported example input from the original action order to the reordered sequence 2, 3, 4, 5, 1. This corrects the example to match the position-control procedure already described in v2; it does not establish a rerun. Main evaluation budgets, metrics, sampling settings, and human-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The time-limit sensitivity, human comparisons, attention analyses and interventions, decomposition controls, positional tests, and four case studies already appear in v2. Their analytical questions and supporting results remain unchanged. The expanded Section 5.3.4 principally summarizes existing Appendix C.4 evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 repetitions per task, 20 tests per sampled scenario in the failure analysis, matched seeds for attention interventions, and Pearson correlations with p-values in Figure 12. No statistical reporting or uncertainty-estimation practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: New Claude Sonnet 4 and o4-mini results change the performance leader: their Level 6 success rates are 58% and 54%, versus DeepSeek-R1's retained 30%. Table 2 also corrects Qwen2.5-32B's Level 5 SR from 2.18 to 2.00 and Llama-3.1-70B's Level 4 SR from 6.18 to 6.00. Other retained results and appendix findings remain stable.

T1.justification: Equations (2) and (8) correct the final alignment constraint from a_{i_k} = g_k to a_{i_d} = g_d. This makes the condition correspond to the quantified matched length d rather than the agent index k. The remaining mathematical framework is unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain the 30-task benchmark, initiation/response decomposition, trajectory-based evaluation metrics, and identification of collaboration and attention bottlenecks. Updating the abstract, introduction, and conclusion from 11 to 13 evaluated LLMs expands supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies v2's broad collapse-at-high-complexity interpretation by acknowledging that Claude Sonnet 4 and o4-mini postpone the decline. Section 5.3.4 also more strongly attributes degradation to positional biases and context-tracking limitations using existing controls. The stated Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Listing 6 now supplies the reordered recipe and annotations identifying original step positions, improving documentation of the existing control. However, its new Baked Pumpkin Soup title conflicts with its bell-pepper ingredients and actions. Code-access information, detailed agent prompts, and implementation descriptions otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Claude and o4-mini system cards, MAST, AutoBencher, ExpeL, and MultiAgentBench references. It relates the baseline to established agent architectures and positions its quantitative failure analysis relative to MAST. The broader related-work overview and benchmark comparison remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 edits abstract and introduction wording, standardizes model terminology, expands Sections 4.2 and 5.3.4, and adds acknowledgments. It also corrects the reversed Case 2 and Case 3 headings in Appendix C.5. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains two rows and revised emphasis. Figure 3 changes colors, markers, model groupings, and vertical scales; its caption claims 13 models although only 12 are plotted. Appendix tables, listings, and Figure 11 shift position through reflow, while other figure content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional strong comparators test the benchmark's conclusions more broadly and motivate a better-qualified account of performance collapse. Equation, case-heading, and recipe-example corrections improve precision. These gains are limited by Figure 3's missing DeepSeek-R1 and incorrect model count, the recipe-name inconsistency, and stronger causal wording based on unchanged controls.
